top_story.headline: Navy gives its Trident nuclear-missile program three more contracts without competition, all to longtime incumbents
top_story.dek: The Navy's Strategic Systems Programs office posted three sole-source justifications on October 30, citing decades of incumbent expertise and estimated transition costs of up to $183 million.
paragraphs: The Department of the Navy's Strategic Systems Programs office, which manages the Trident II (D5) submarine-launched nuclear missile, posted three justifications on October 30 for continuing work with companies it has used for decades. Each cites 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), meaning the Navy says only one company can do the job, and each calls the new contract a follow-on to the fiscal 2022 to 2026 effort.

BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services, Inc. appears twice. The first justification covers systems engineering and integration across the Trident II weapons system, the Columbia-class submarine missile compartment and the new nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile program. The Navy calls it a direct follow-on to two earlier non-competed BAE contracts, from fiscal 2022 and fiscal 2025. It says competing the work would cause "a delay of a minimum of three years and $183M in duplication of cost during transition" (justification). No dollar value could be verified for this one. The second BAE justification covers facilities acquisition and engineering support for the nuclear weapons infrastructure, October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2031. Its own cost table totals about $78.2 million, and the Navy says BAE has done this work since 1968 and that switching contractors would cost "nearly $39M" (justification). The document says the work was last bought from BAE on a sole-source basis in 2021.

Unified Industries Incorporated gets the third: a firm-fixed-price contract for test, measurement and diagnostic equipment lifecycle support for the Ohio/Vanguard and Columbia/Dreadnought classes of Trident submarines. The justification's table totals $29.93 million over a planned base year starting October 1, 2026 and four option years. The Navy says the company has been the program's lead coordinator since 1977, holds 1,105 calibration artifacts at a Springfield, Virginia facility, and that moving the work to another source would take 12 to 18 months (justification).

sections.headline: Veterans Affairs sole-sources a $38 million, five-year residential mental health contract to its Connecticut incumbent
paragraphs: There were 23 new sole-source justifications, 13 of them posted under other notice types (Special Notice, Sources Sought and Award Notice), and 2 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The three Trident justifications are in the Top Story and four extensions and bridges are in the Extensions section; the rest is mostly routine.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs gives Connecticut residential mental health contract to its incumbent for $38 million without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification covers a new five-year contract, November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2031, for 18 residential rehabilitation beds at $635 a bed-day and 10 PTSD residential beds at $938 a bed-day for veterans of the VA Connecticut Healthcare System. The agency says the beds must be within a 10 to 15 minute drive of the West Haven campus so its clinicians can reach patients quickly, and that the company has provided the beds since 2021. The file properties list the author as "VHAPROWellsK"; nothing in them points to the vendor.
Also worth a look

items: Coast Guard buys a two-day offshore support vessel charter for its West Coast security response team from Eclipse Group without competition. The statement of work asks for a U.S.-flagged vessel of at least 170 feet for boat and helicopter insertion training on November 5 and 6, 2026, and the value is not stated. It was posted as a Special Notice. (34269PR270000001)

Veterans Affairs plans to buy DistillerSR, an AI-assisted literature-review platform, on a brand-name-or-equal basis. The draft work statement is for five Evidence Synthesis Program centers and lists Executive Order 14319, "Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government," among its applicable documents. It was posted as a Sources Sought notice with no value stated. (36C10B27Q0085)

Veterans Affairs plans to keep Draeger as sole maintainer of anesthesia equipment for its Network 23 medical centers. The notice of intent covers a base year plus two option years, value not stated, and was posted as a Special Notice. (36C26327Q0049)

U.S. Marshals Service gives RBEX Inc. $500,000 to tow, store and dispose of seized vehicles in Kentucky, Ohio, West Virginia and western Pennsylvania without competition. The pipeline has logged two earlier Marshals Service vehicle-services justifications for this vendor, covering Nevada and Hawaii. (15M50027DA4400-TBD-20261030)

sections.headline: Missile Defense Agency extends Raytheon's radar-support contract two more years and adds $489.86 million
paragraphs: There are four new extensions or bridges: two Defense Department cards below and two staffing bridge modifications.

blocks.title: Missile Defense Agency extends Raytheon's X-band radar support contract through October 2028 and adds $489.86 million without competition
meta: follow-on to the original maker (delay otherwise unacceptable)
blocks.text: The amended justification extends the ordering period of the contractor logistics support contract for the AN/TPY-2 missile-defense radars two years, to October 31, 2028, and raises the maximum value by $489.86 million to $3.095 billion. The contract began as a sole-source award on October 17, 2017, ran four one-year options through October 2024, and was extended two years in 2024 (adding $859.731 million). The agency says it added a 25% buffer to its cost estimate for unknown real-world events. It says the Army is taking over missile defense operations, and the extension lets the Army update requirements and award its own contract.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency bridges SOS International's Indo-Pacific coalition network contract on the day it expires
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The bridge covers engineering and operations for U.S. Indo-Pacific Command's Mission Partner Environment, a secret-level network for sharing information with allies. The current task order expires October 31, 2026, with a six-month base plus a six-month option and a follow-on award expected within 12 months. The agency says SOS International is the only contractor with vetted personnel and host-nation base access credentials at all overseas sites, and that no market research report was required for a bridge.

items: ServeFed, Inc. gets a bridge modification for Clinical East staffing services valued at $19,978,602 without competition while the follow-on acquisition is completed. The notice lists no agency and its document was not read. (HHSP233201800009I_75P00123F37008)
